encounter_greeting.text: Hold, ser {player}. You stand before {persona} of {my_faction}, and I remind you that this road belongs to those who keep their oaths.
Greetings, traveller. I am {persona} of {my_faction}. State your business plainly and I shall weigh it honestly, as my ancestors taught me.
Ser {player}, what a joy to see your banner upon this road. Let us speak as old allies should, with bread and words between us.
Ser {player}, I am {persona} of {my_faction}. The oaths of Dolmare do not bend for the idle, so mark your steps before you take another.

encounter_threatened.text: You name a price and threaten my steel, ser {player}? Then hear me. {persona} does not pay {gold} to a man who forgets his oath. Draw, if you dare.
Ser {player}, you ask {gold} of me under threat. A keeper of the Gravel Gate does not surrender for coin. Speak again with honour, or leave me to my road.
Ser {player}, I know you jest, but you have named {gold} and a blade in one breath. Withdraw the threat and we shall call this a misunderstanding.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Ser {player}, I accept your proposal of alliance. Against {enemy_faction} we shall stand together, and I shall hold you to every word spoken upon this road.
Ser {player}, my hand is yours. We shall ride against {enemy_faction} as one, and let the saga record that {persona} never broke faith with a friend.
Very well, ser {player}. Bind your banner to mine against {enemy_faction}. Yet mark me, I shall not share a campfire with {rival} while my oath stands.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. An alliance sworn in haste is a grave built on sand, and I will not lay my name beside yours. Go with what dignity you have left.
I must refuse you, ser {player}. My oath to the Gravel Gate forbids binding myself to any banner I have not weighed for a full season.
Ser {player}, you ask me to ally with you while {rival} still walks free with my grievances unanswered. I refuse, and I shall not pretend otherwise.
Forgive me, ser {player}, but I cannot take your hand in alliance this day. Ask again when the road is kinder, and I shall listen gladly.

captured_by_player.text: You have taken me, ser {player}, and I shall not weep before you. {my_faction} will remember this hour, and the debt shall be paid in full.
Ser {player}, I yield my sword to you as a captive, not as a coward. Name your ransom of {gold} and let the matter be settled with honour.
Well struck, ser {player}. I am your prisoner and bear no grudge, for a fair fight deserves a fair captivity. Treat my men with mercy, I beg you.
Bind me then, ser {player}. {my_faction} shall sing of this day, and the song shall be no praise for your cunning.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you loosed my chains without asking for coin. I shall repay that mercy in full when the road gives me the chance.
Ser {player} has spared me the cells and asked nothing in return. A rare mercy on these roads, and I shall not forget it.
Ser {player}, you let me go when a ransom would have served you. I still count you an enemy, but I am no longer in your debt for a cell.
Ser {player} released me rather than name a ransom. Mercy from a rival is a strange gift, and I shall weigh it carefully.

player_left_my_faction.text: Ser {player} has forsworn {my_faction} for {faction}. A broken oath is a stain that does not wash out, and the saga will remember it.
Ser {player}, you have left {my_faction} for {faction}. I shall not curse your name, but a sworn word given so lightly is a sad thing to see.
Ser {player}, you walked from {my_faction} to {faction} like a man changing cloaks. Honour is not a garment, and I think you know it.
{faction} has gained a sword and {my_faction} has lost one. Let the record show that ser {player} made their choice and must bear it.

war_declared.text: Let it be sung across Ormerath that {my_faction} has declared war upon {enemy_faction}. The oaths are broken and the swords are drawn.
Heralds of {my_faction} have named {enemy_faction} as our foe. Our ancestors watch this day, and we shall not make them ashamed.
{enemy_faction} stands declared our enemy. Let no lord claim later that he did not swear this oath at council.
Steel is drawn between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. May the saga record who kept faith and who did not.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player} stood beside me with {troop_count} blades against {enemy_faction}, and the field was ours. Such deeds are sung for generations.
Ser {player}, your {troop_count} men held the line at my side. Had you faltered, the day would have gone to {enemy_faction}. I am grateful.
Ser {player}, with {troop_count} of your banner we broke {enemy_faction} at the ford. I shall remember that the day was won by honest steel.
{troop_count} of ser {player}'s troops fought well against {enemy_faction}. A fair showing, and one worth a toast at council.

encounter_farewell.text: Fare well, ser {player}. May your road be straight and your oaths be kept, for I doubt you would have it otherwise.
Go in peace, ser {player}. We have spoken plainly, and plain speech is the bread of honest men. Until we meet again upon the road.
Begone, ser {player}. Our paths part for now, but I have not forgotten the grievance and neither has the saga.
Ser {player}, the council bell calls me back to my post. Safe travels, and may your word prove as firm as the stones of Dolmare.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has fallen on the road to {town} for three days, and the mud has swallowed half a cart. Still, the saga does not pause for weather.
Has anyone seen the sun since the morning bell in {village}? I should like to swear my oath beneath a clear sky, if only for once.
The walls of {town} were raised by my ancestors' hands and they still stand. Any lord who doubts that stone should walk its length at dusk.
The bread and ale at {village} are the finest on the Orlagua road. I will hear no argument from anyone who has not tasted them.
